headline: Desert Lagoons, Sky Mirrors & Ice Walls
editorial_intent: A genuinely useful cross-border South America collection presenting five distinct extraordinary, geographically verified landscape experiences instead of one generic destination.
reader_scenario: Traveller discovering natural phenomena and unusual scenic places worth travelling to in South America.
share_reason: Distinct natural contrasts from Brazilian rain-filled dunes to Bolivian mirrored salt, Peruvian oasis, Chilean lunar rock and Argentinian glacier inspire saves and discussion.
slide_count_rationale: Five different countries and five independently verified surprising landscapes in five portrait photographs; no filler outro.
caption:
South America really does have landscapes that seem made up. 🌎

📍 Lençóis Maranhenses, Brazil — seasonal freshwater lagoons appear between endless sand dunes.
📍 Salar de Uyuni, Bolivia — in the wet season, a thin layer of water can turn salt flats into a giant sky mirror.
📍 Huacachina, Peru — a palm-ringed desert oasis surrounded by huge dunes.
📍 Valle de la Luna, Chile — eroded red rock and sand resemble another planet.
📍 Perito Moreno, Argentina — towering blue glacier walls beside a glacial lake.

Save these for a South American adventure.

Photos: Marcus Dall Col, Susanne Feldt, Willian Justen de Vasconcellos & Hans-Jürgen Weinhardt / Unsplash.
